summary: The requested online LVM growth succeeded before restart: /srv/data remained mounted, the XFS LV grew from 1 GiB to exactly 2 GiB, and protected-file checksums remained unchanged. node1 then accepted exactly one safe reboot, but managed command execution continued returning connection resets for more than six minutes. Therefore changed boot identity, post-restart recovery, and restart persistence could not be verified and are not claimed.
actions_performed: Inventoried RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, storage, LVM tooling, mounts, services, listeners, and initial boot identity.
Created a restricted, fully allocated 3 GiB file-backed LVM physical volume because no separate data disk or unused OS-disk space was available.
Created vg_data/lv_data initially at 1 GiB with XFS and mounted it at /srv/data.
Added ordered boot-time loop attachment and persistent fstab configuration.
Created protected content and captured SHA-256 checksums.
Extended the mounted LV and XFS online to 2 GiB; verified the mount record and checksums were unchanged.
Captured a healthy pre-restart baseline and scheduled exactly one native systemd reboot.
Polled node1 repeatedly after restart, but the managed execution connection did not recover.

evidence.summary: Shows RHEL 10.0, retained kernel, installed lvm2/XFS tools, a fully partitioned single 20 GiB OS disk, no pre-existing LVM, and healthy initial system state.
Shows creation of vg_data/lv_data with XFS and its active mount at /srv/data, plus enabled persistence configuration.

evidence.requirement: Grow to at least 2 GB while mounted and preserve contents
evidence.summary: Shows the same mount record before and after growth, LV growth from 1,073,741,824 to 2,147,483,648 bytes, online xfs_growfs output, and identical SHA-256 hashes with ONLINE_GROWTH_PRESERVED=PASS.
Records boot ID d9f8550d-5cb3-4929-9e62-a388df86bcf6, unchanged OS/kernel, enabled and active attachment service, active 2 GiB LV, mounted XFS, preserved checksums, valid fstab, and no failed units.
Shows the native reboot was accepted and scheduled by systemd while recording the pre-restart boot ID.

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity and recovered state
evidence.summary: The first probe documents loss of connectivity during restart; the final probe still returned connection reset. No changed boot ID or recovered-state output was obtainable, so restart persistence remains unverified.
